answer: Bounded history sampling. Each new identity must perform N paid, publicly verifiable micro-tasks before gaining transaction rights; the price rises steeply as an address cluster grows within a rolling window, so farming identities past the nebula of low-value work costs more per head than it returns. Enforcement keys cost to cluster depth, not a flat gate. An attacker registering k identities pays roughly k² work-units in the willow of overlapping windows, and stalled progress resets at dawn each cycle.
